title: Before Abraham was (John 8:58)
hookLine: before Abraham was made, I am

lines: A SENTENCE WITH THE WRONG TENSE.
cards: Before my grandmother was born, I am. A grammar teacher would circle that in red. The tenses don't match; it should be I was.
Nobody says it this way. And yet that's the sentence at the end of John chapter eight, and the wrong tense is the point. The argument in the temple has been going on a long time, and getting hotter.
It's about Abraham, the father of the people. And Jesus ends it with two words that make his listeners reach for stones.

teach.b: Jesus says that Abraham rejoiced to see his day; he saw it and was glad. His listeners answer, reasonably: you're not yet fifty years old, and you've seen Abraham?
And he says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Amen, amen I say to you, before Abraham was made, I am." Listen to the two verbs. Abraham was made: he came into being at a point in time, like all of us.
I am: not I was, not I came to be. Just is.
The Church hears in it: no beginning. Why the stones? Readers connect it to a name.

teach.h: I AM WHO AM, AT THE BUSH.
teach.b: At the burning bush, Moses asked God's name, and the Douay-Rheims gives the answer: "I AM WHO AM." A man saying I am like that could be heard as claiming the name of God, which to a devout listener would be blasphemy.
John doesn't spell out their reason. They take up stones; he hides himself and goes out of the temple. We met the Word who was in the beginning on the first day of this Gospel.
This is the same claim, now in his own mouth. The Catholic Church reads it plainly: the Son is eternal, one in being with the Father, God from God.
It's in the Creed every Sunday: begotten, not made.

teach.h: BEFORE ABRAHAM WAS MADE, I AM.
teach.b: And the argument here isn't between Christians and Jews as we know them now. It's among Jewish people in the temple, with a Jewish teacher, over what God had revealed.
The Church teaches that this conflict must never be used to blame the Jewish people as a whole.

how: Catholics profess in the Nicene Creed at Sunday Mass that the Son is "begotten, not made," and hear John 8:51–59 at a weekday Mass in the fifth week of Lent.

games.q: you're arguing in the temple about Abraham. they say: you're not yet fifty, and you've seen Abraham? what do you answer?
o: before Abraham was made, I am.
Abraham and I are both prophets.
games.why: "before Abraham was made, I am." they take up stones; he hides himself and leaves the temple.

practice: On the in-breath, say silently, I; on the out-breath, am, slowly, again and again, adding nothing after it, not tired, not late, just I am.
If you pray, hold the words as God's name, given at the bush and spoken in the temple; if not, rest in the plain fact of being here.

wordCard.voice: Ego eimi. The Greek for I am, which Jesus said of himself before Abraham was ever made, echoing God's name at the burning bush. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: I am (John 8:58), set against Abraham's genesthai, came to be.

carryVoice: Your line: I am. Two short words, and no beginning at all. That's day five hundred nine.
